diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: All downward arrows are images under pi:X -> C-hat. p_j=(a_j,0), j=1,...,6; b is finite and avoids these six values, s^2=P(b), b_+=(b,s), b_-=(b,-s); infinity_+ and infinity_- are the two completion-chart points.
checks: Distinct roots make P prime(a_j) nonzero. Step 1.1 gives local expression y -> y^2 w_j(y), w_j(0) nonzero; the ramification-index definition and step 5.1 therefore justify index 2 on exactly each p_j -> a_j arrow. There are exactly six such arrows, one for each root.
P(b) is nonzero, hence s and -s are distinct; step 6.1 identifies the two-point fibre over b, and step 5.1 gives index 1 at both points.
Step 2.1 has two distinct infinity charts v=+rho(t), v=-rho(t), rho(0) nonzero, with projection t -> t. Thus both infinity arrows have index 1, and infinity is not a branch value.
Every shown fibre has total index 2 as in F11 and step 6.1. The six contributions e-1 each equal 1, and all other contributions vanish; F12 and step 7.1 give 2g(X)-2=2(-2)+6=2.
Horizontal coordinates only separate labelled fibres: the figure asserts no real ordering of the complex a_j, no paths between them and no global splitting into sheets.

diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: Psi:D -> X; pi:X -> C-hat; q:D -> D/Gamma, z -> [z]; Phi:D/Gamma -> X, [z] -> Psi(z).
checks: Step 9.1 defines Psi=p composed with psi inverse and identifies its deck group Gamma; step 10.1 proves the Gamma action properly discontinuous and step 9.1 proves it free.
Step 10.4 proves Psi(gamma z)=Psi(z), so Phi is well defined and Phi composed with q equals Psi; these are exactly the two paths from D to X in the drawn triangle.
Step 10.4 proves Phi is a homeomorphism by deck transitivity, quotient continuity and openness. The figure labels only Phi as a homeomorphism, never pi or Psi.
Step 6.1 gives degree(pi)=2. The rightward pi arrow targets the sphere, a separate object from X; it is the branched map, while Psi is the unramified universal covering.
